title: The tangential connection of a submanifold
promptMarkdown:
Let $(N,h)$ be a Riemannian manifold, $M\subseteq N$ a submanifold with the induced metric $g$, and $
abla$ the Levi-Civita connection of $(N,h)$. For vector fields $	ilde X,	ilde Y$ on $M$ with local extensions $X,Y$ to $N$, define
$$	ilde
abla_{	ilde X}	ilde Y=(
abla_XY)^	op,\qquad B(	ilde X,	ilde Y)=(
abla_XY)^\perp$$
along $M$. You may take as known (Remark 6.18) that these do not depend on the extensions chosen.

1. Prove that $	ilde
abla$ is a connection on $TM$.
2. Prove that $	ilde
abla$ is torsion-free. (You will need that $[X,Y]$ is tangent to $M$ along $M$ and restricts to $[	ilde X,	ilde Y]$; prove this, for instance in a slice chart.)
3. Prove that $	ilde
abla$ is compatible with $g$.
4. Conclude from the fundamental theorem that $	ilde
abla$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $(M,g)$ (this is Theorem 6.20 of the notes), and show that $B$ is symmetric.
5. Apply this to $S^2_R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ with $
abla=\partial$ the directional derivative: show that for tangent fields $X,Y$ and $p\in S^2_R$,
$$	ilde
abla_XY=\partial_XY+ rac{1}{R^2}\langle X,Yangle\,p,\qquad B(X,Y)=- rac{1}{R^2}\langle X,Yangle\,p .$$
hintLadder: Tangential projection $v\mapsto v^\top$ is linear on each $T_pN$; what does that give for $\tilde\nabla_{\tilde X}(f\tilde Y)$ once you extend $f$ to $N$?
In a slice chart $M=\{x^{m+1}=\dots=x^n=0\}$, tangency of $X$ to $M$ means $X^\alpha=0$ on $M$ for $\alpha>m$. Compute $[X,Y]^\alpha$ on $M$.
For compatibility: $\tilde Xg(\tilde Y,\tilde Z)=Xh(Y,Z)$ along $M$; expand with the ambient compatibility and use that $Z$ is tangent to kill the normal part.
For the sphere, the normal space at $p$ is $\mathbb{R}p$. Differentiate the identity $\langle Y,p\rangle=0$ along $X$, remembering that $\partial_X$ of the position vector field is $X$.

checkExamples.label: correct LaTeX sphere formula
checkExamples.text: Along $S^2_R$ we have $\langle Y,p\rangle=0$, so $0=X\langle Y,p\rangle=\langle\partial_XY,p\rangle+\langle Y,X\rangle$ and $(\partial_XY)^\perp=\frac{1}{R^2}\langle\partial_XY,p\rangle p=-\frac{1}{R^2}\langle X,Y\rangle p$. Hence $\tilde\nabla_XY=\partial_XY+\frac{1}{R^2}\langle X,Y\rangle p$ and $B(X,Y)=-\frac{1}{R^2}\langle X,Y\rangle p$.

checkExamples.label: plain-text sphere formula
checkExamples.text: The tangential connection is D_X Y + (1/R^2) <X,Y> p and the second fundamental form is -(1/R^2) <X,Y> p.

checkExamples.label: sign error
checkExamples.text: We get the tangential connection D_X Y - (1/R^2) <X,Y> p on the sphere.

difficulty.basis: A full proof of Theorem 6.20 organised around the fundamental theorem (connection axioms, torsion through a slice-chart bracket argument, compatibility) and the sphere formulas, drawing on the induced metric and the sphere of unit 1.
